items.prompt: Inheritance reads as which sentence?
choices: X is a kind of Y
X holds a Y
X was copied from Y
items.explanation: Inheritance says a subclass is a kind of its parent.

items.prompt: A car has an engine. Which model fits that sentence?
choices: Inheritance, because a car is an engine
Composition, because a car has an engine
Inheritance, because a car needs an engine
items.explanation: "Has-a" is composition: the engine is a part the car holds.

items.prompt: How many parent classes can a class extend under single inheritance?
choices: Two
Any number
One
items.explanation: Single inheritance allows exactly one parent.

items.prompt: In composition, where does an object's behavior come from?
choices: Parts handed to it
A parent class it extends
A global it reads
items.explanation: Composition assembles behavior from parts given to the object.

items.prompt: A SavingsAccount is a kind of Account differing only in interest. Which fits best?
choices: Composition, with a set of loose parts
Inheritance, in a small shallow tree
A full copy of the Account code
items.explanation: One stable axis and a true is-a suit a small inheritance tree.

items.prompt: What is the strategy pattern?
choices: Making every class extend one base class
Copying a method
Handing in a swappable behavior
items.explanation: Strategy hands in the behavior instead of hardcoding it.

items.prompt: Which sentence describes a has-a relationship?
choices: A mage is a character
A character has a speed
A warrior is a character
items.explanation: Holding a speed as a part is has-a. The other two are is-a.

items.prompt: What did the Battle Mage request need that a one-parent tree cannot give?
choices: Two attack styles at once
A faster attack
A different character name
items.explanation: The tree allows one branch per class, but the request needs two.

items.prompt: A `Report` class extends `Printer` just to reuse its print code. What is wrong with this design?
choices: A report is not a printer; it should be given one instead
Reports can never print themselves, whatever design is used
Printer must always be an interface and never a class here
Report should extend two printers to be safe
items.explanation: The is-a sentence is false, so the code is borrowed through inheritance for convenience. Handing the report a printer says what is true: a report has a printer.
items.reference:
Two ways to relate objects
inheritance: reads "is-a", behavior comes from a parent class
composition: reads "has-a", behavior comes from parts handed in
inheritance fits one stable axis; composition fits several traits mixed per object
Why: inheritance commits to one dimension of variation, composition lets several combine.
items.learnMore:
Is-a versus has-a

Ask whether the sentence "X is a Y" is true by nature, and whether X differs from other Ys in only one stable way. If yes, a small tree is simple. If X needs a mix of independent traits, hand it parts instead.

Common mistake

Using inheritance only to reuse code. A Report that extends Printer to print itself is not a printer, so it should be given one.
items.reflection: Think of something you own or a role you hold. Which of its traits are what it is, and which are things it has that could be swapped?

items.prompt: A shallow tree has `SavingsAccount` and `CheckingAccount`; only interest differs and no other trait is expected. A reviewer demands composition. Best response?

Inheritance is always right, so composition must never be used
The tree must be split into one class per customer
items.explanation: Composition solves multi-axis problems. With one stable axis, it adds indirection without removing any cost.

items.prompt: What shape does single inheritance form?
choices: A cycle
A tree
A grid
items.explanation: Each class has one parent, so classes form a tree.

items.prompt: In a tree, how many paths lead from a node back to the root?
choices: Exactly one
Two or three
None at all
items.explanation: A tree has one path from any node up to the root.

items.prompt: What would BattleMage have to extend to get both attacks?
choices: Character and nothing else
Mage, ignoring Warrior
Warrior and Mage together
items.explanation: It would need two parents, which single inheritance does not allow.

items.prompt: How many axes of variation does a tree of only Warrior and Mage have?
choices: One
Two
Three
items.explanation: Only the attack style varies, so there is one axis.

items.prompt: Why does pasting Mage's spell code into a Warrior subclass go wrong?
choices: The compiler rejects the second copy of it
Two copies must now be kept in sync
Spells become weaker
items.explanation: Two copies of one rule drift apart when one is changed.

items.prompt: Does implementing two interfaces give a class two inherited implementations?
choices: Yes, with full code for both of them
Yes, but only for spells
No, it declares only a contract
items.explanation: Interfaces carry the contract. The code still has to be written in the class.

items.prompt: In composition, what is a Battle Mage?
choices: A character given melee and magic parts
A new subclass extending both parents at once
A new base class
items.explanation: No special class is needed: it is a character holding both parts.

items.prompt: Which pair are two independent axes?
choices: Warrior and Mage, the two subclasses
Movement style and attack style
Attack and damage number
items.explanation: Each can change without the other, such as flying with magic or walking with magic.

items.prompt: A tree has `Warrior` and `Mage` under `Character`. Which new request can it absorb cleanly?
choices: An Archer that attacks only with a bow, no spells
A Battle Mage that swings a sword and casts spells
A character choosing melee or magic each fight
A Healer that casts spells and also fights with a club
items.explanation: A new single-style type is just another branch. The other requests each need two attack styles on one class.
items.reference:
A tree has one path to the root
one axis (attack style): each subclass picks one branch, which fits
two axes (movement and attack): the class must reach two branches at once
an interface declares a contract but does not carry the code
Why: the tree shape allows one parent, so the shape has to change, not the rules about who may extend whom.
items.learnMore:
Why a tree cannot hold two axes

Single inheritance gives every class exactly one parent. A second independent trait needs a second parent, or a copy of the code. The copy creates two sources of truth for one rule.

Common mistake

Thinking multiple interfaces solve it. Interfaces carry only the contract, so the implementation still has to be written somewhere.
items.reflection: Think of a category you use that works by sorting things into one box each. What kind of item would belong in two boxes at once?

Warrior characters start casting spells by accident
Mage must now extend BattleMage to stay consistent
items.explanation: The copy does not fail loudly. It silently drifts, leaving two sources of truth for one rule.

items.prompt: With 3 movement and 3 attack styles, how many components does composition need?
items.explanation: 3 + 3 = 6, one part per style.

items.prompt: With 3 movement and 3 attack styles, how many subclasses cover every pairing?
items.explanation: 3 x 3 = 9, one subclass per pairing.

items.prompt: A new attack style under composition costs how much?
choices: One per movement style
One new component
Nothing at all
items.explanation: Each style is one part, whatever else exists.

items.prompt: A new attack style under per-combo inheritance needs one new subclass for each what?
choices: Existing movement style
Existing attack style in the game
Existing player
items.explanation: Each movement style pairs with the new attack style, so each needs a subclass.

items.prompt: At 5 styles on each of two axes, how many components does composition need?
At 5 styles on each of two axes, how many subclasses does per-combo inheritance need?
Which formula is composition's cost for two axes of n and m styles?
choices: n + m
n x m
n ^ m
items.explanation: Parts are added, not multiplied.

items.prompt: Which grows faster as styles are added to both axes?
choices: Adding, as in n + m, in every case
Multiplying, as in n x m
They grow identically
items.explanation: Products pull away from sums as n and m grow.

items.prompt: A game has 4 movement styles and 4 attack styles. Which pair of counts is right?
choices: 16 components with composition; 8 subclasses per pairing
8 components with composition; 8 subclasses per pairing
8 components with composition; 16 subclasses per pairing
4 components with composition; 16 subclasses per pairing
items.explanation: Composition adds 4 + 4 = 8. A subclass per pairing multiplies 4 x 4 = 16.
items.reference:
Two axes of n styles each
n = 1: composition 2, per-combo 1
n = 2: composition 4, per-combo 4 (they tie)
n = 3: composition 6, per-combo 9
n = 5: composition 10, per-combo 25
third axis of 3 on a 3 x 3 game: 6 to 9 parts, 9 to 27 subclasses
Why: composition adds one part per style, per-combo inheritance multiplies by every axis.
items.learnMore:
Adding versus multiplying

With composition, each new style is one new part whatever else exists. With a subclass per pairing, each new style needs a subclass for every style on the other axes, and each new axis multiplies the total.

Common mistake

Reading the tie at 2 x 2 as proof that nothing matters until 3. The rate of new work per future change already differs from the first added style.

Whenever the program has a great many classes
Never; composition should always be used

Names like FlyingBattleMage piling up
Builds that get a lot faster

items.prompt: Which is over-correcting?

Injecting behaviors once two axes must combine
Noticing the second axis early
items.explanation: Extra indirection without a second axis only adds cost.

A swappable behavior

items.prompt: A third axis (defense) under composition adds what to the constructor shape?

A new base class

items.prompt: A tree has `SavingsAccount` and `CheckingAccount`; only interest differs. An engineer proposes an injected interest strategy. Best judgement?

Required, since inheritance is unsafe in every possible case
Harmful, because injected parts cannot hold interest rules at all

items.explanation: Composition earns its cost when axes multiply. One stable axis does not need it, yet the design should be revisited if another axis shows up.

What the rewrite does and does not prove
behaviors are data handed in as a list; a Battle Mage is a longer list
a third axis adds one list and its parts, not a new subclass per pairing

Why: match the tool to whether there is one axis or more than one.
items.learnMore:
Composition in the rewrite

The character class stores lists of behavior functions and iterates them. Supporting a new trait means adding a field and some parts. Supporting a new combination means passing different lists.

Common mistake

Composing every class by reflex. A single stable axis, like savings versus checking accounts, does not need the extra indirection.

items.explanation: Composition needs one part per style, so the counts add.

items.prompt: Implement `countSubclasses(moves, attacks)`: how many subclasses are needed to cover every pairing.
items.explanation: Each movement style pairs with each attack style, so the counts multiply.

items.prompt: Implement `describe(name, behavior)`: call `behavior()` and return the name, a space, then its result.

tests.expr: expect(describe("Kade", () => "swings a sword")).toBe("Kade swings a sword")
expect(describe("Zara", () => "casts a fireball")).toBe("Zara casts a fireball")

items.explanation: The behavior is just a function handed in, so the caller decides what it does.

items.prompt: Implement `attackAll(name, behaviors)`: return an array with one `name + " " + behavior()` string per behavior.
items.explanation: Mapping over the list handles one behavior or many with the same code.

items.prompt: Implement `countComponents3(a, b, c)`: parts composition needs for three axes with a, b and c styles.
items.explanation: A third axis adds its own styles to the total.

items.prompt: Implement `countSubclasses3(a, b, c)`: subclasses needed to cover every combination of three axes.
items.explanation: A third axis multiplies the existing total by its own style count.

items.prompt: Implement `hasMultipleStyles(behaviors)`: return true when the list holds two or more behaviors.
items.explanation: A Battle Mage is just a list with more than one behavior.

items.prompt: Implement `addBehavior(list, behavior)`: return a new array with `behavior` added at the end, leaving `list` unchanged.

tests.expr: const f = () => 1; const old = [f]; const next = addBehavior(old, () => 2); expect(next.length).toBe(2)

items.explanation: Returning a new array keeps any character that shares the old list unaffected.

items.prompt: Implement `makeCharacter(name, moves, attacks)` returning an object with `move()` and `attack()`. Each returns an array with one `name + " " + behavior()` string per stored behavior, in order. An empty list gives an empty array.
items.explanation: Both actions are the same map over a stored list, so a character with two attacks or none needs no extra code or class.
items.reference:
Building a character from parts
parts are plain functions; the character stores lists of them
an action maps over a list and prefixes each result with the name
an empty list gives an empty result, with no special case
adding a part returns a new list instead of changing the old one
Why: when behavior is data, the class needs no knowledge of how many behaviors there are.
items.learnMore:
Writing the composed character

Each action is a map over the stored list. The empty case works because mapping an empty array returns an empty array. Returning new lists keeps characters that share the old list unaffected.

Common mistake

items.prompt: Implement `makeCharacter(name, parts)` where `parts` maps an axis name to a list of behaviors. Return an object with `perform(axis)` giving one `name + " " + behavior()` string per behavior on that axis, or `[]` if the axis is missing.
items.explanation: A new axis is just a new key, so adding defense needs no change to the character code.
items.reference:
Building a character from parts
parts are plain functions; the character stores lists of them
an action maps over a list and prefixes each result with the name
an empty list gives an empty result, with no special case
adding a part returns a new list instead of changing the old one
Why: when behavior is data, the class needs no knowledge of how many behaviors there are.
items.learnMore:
Writing the composed character

Each action is a map over the stored list. The empty case works because mapping an empty array returns an empty array. Returning new lists keeps characters that share the old list unaffected.
